summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fevers and hypotension during dialysis, found to have MRSA bacteremia likely originating from his right femoral dialysis catheter. He was treated with vancomycin and initially retained the line despite purulence, but developed hypotension requiring MICU care. The infected catheter was removed, followed by a temporary line and two line holidays due to persistent positive cultures. Surveillance cultures eventually cleared, and a new tunneled left femoral dialysis catheter was placed. Echocardiograms showed no evidence of endocarditis, and heart function remained stable. The patient completed antibiotic therapy with vancomycin dosed through dialysis, and was discharged to an extended care facility on a four-week course with weekly monitoring of CBC and vancomycin levels. He restarted lisinopril and continued management of comorbidities including ESRD, systolic heart failure, and seizure disorder.
